text: I will interpret the water volume as the annular chamber from the 12 mm hub radius to the 58 mm radial exit, between the backplate top at \(z=4\) mm and shroud at \(z=18\) mm. The axial inlet is the annulus \(r=12\)–16 mm in the shroud opening; this resolves the phrase “hub bore” against the specified solid 12 mm-radius hub. I will use a swept, constant-thickness blade profile whose centreline retreats 30° over \(r=16\)–58 mm, replicate it sevenfold, subtract the blades from the fluid envelope, export face-derived named patches, then use a coarse snappyHexMesh before refinement. I will initially omit the 2 mm blade-root fillets because the first coarse cells will be comparable to them, as the request permits.

I am now constructing the nominal fluid solid in metres. The blade centreline uses a smooth monotone polar law from 16 to 58 mm while its azimuth retreats exactly 30°; the 3 mm planform thickness is formed by a symmetric offset. The blade solids span the full 14 mm passage height, so omitting the root fillets is geometrically explicit rather than an accidental loss during meshing.

The first replication expression returned build123d’s location-list wrapper rather than individual solids, so that cell is not reproducible and will not be retained. I will rebuild the same geometry with explicit immutable `Location` transforms.

The measured vertical extent exposed a build123d `Location` constructor ambiguity: the three-tuple was interpreted as rotation data, shifting the result incorrectly. I will inspect the installed constructor and replace it with its explicit position argument before any export.
I will verify explicit vector translation separately so the corrected construction has a measured \(z=4\)–18 mm extent.
`Location(Vector)` is likewise not a pure translation in this release. I will use build123d’s explicit `Pos` location-list element and test its single location directly.
`Pos` itself is the immutable location, not a list; I will apply it directly.
The translation is functioning, but this reveals that `Cylinder` is centred by default in this installed API. I will inspect and explicitly set its axial alignment instead of relying on a default.
I will correct the envelope with explicit minimum-\(z\) alignment, reconstruct the final fluid shape, and remeasure its bounds and volume.

Four faces means the blade subtraction did not intersect the corrected envelope, despite the unchanged total volume confirming that suspicion. I will inspect the blade’s vertical bounds; this is another placement/alignment issue to correct before preview.
The offset-generated sketch is empty in this API path. I will inspect the centreline and offset object counts, then switch to an explicit closed blade polygon if necessary.
The offset contains a valid closed curve but not a face, so extrusion silently produced no solid. I will convert its closed wire to a `Face`, then extrude and verify blade thickness and bounds.

Agreed. I will freeze the corrected no-fillet shape now, classify its boundary faces by analytic surface type, export all six patches in one welded tessellation call, and proceed immediately to a very coarse snappy mesh.

The exporter correctly rejected the top because the inlet and shroud were still one unsplit CAD face. I will resolve this in the geometry (not by relabelling triangles): add a minimal 2 mm axial inlet neck over the \(12\)–16 mm annulus. This produces a true axial inlet face at \(z=20\) mm and a true shroud face at \(z=18\) mm; the neck’s outer wall belongs to the shroud and its inner wall to the hub.
I will re-emit the successful export step with all previously refused-cell names defined locally, so `build.py` can replay it from empty.

The closed six-patch surface is now on disk. I will create a coarse Cartesian background mesh with about 5 mm in-plane and 4 mm axial spacing, then snap/refine each named surface once (about 2.5 mm locally). This is intentionally too coarse for 2 mm root fillets, confirming their omission.
I will run `blockMesh` and `snappyHexMesh -overwrite` now, then inspect the mesher’s termination and cell count before rendering.
The first mesher call failed immediately on dictionary syntax, not geometry. I will print the generated block dictionary and correct its compact formatting.
OpenFOAM requires whitespace between adjacent parenthesized list entries. I will rewrite only `blockMeshDict` in standard multiline form and rerun both stages.
The coarse background mesh now exists (4,056 cells). Snappy stopped while reading its dictionary; I will inspect the exact parser error from the saved log and fix that dictionary only.

Snappy’s mesh-motion stage requires minimal `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` files even though no flow solve is being configured. I will add only the standard meshing entries and rerun from the existing background mesh.
Geometry loading succeeded; the remaining stop is after feature setup. I will inspect the final fatal message.
The compact token `features();` was not parsed as an entry. I will replace it with `features ();`, reset the background mesh because the failed run may have touched it, and rerun.
A coarse snapped mesh now exists with 1,281 cells. I will run the binding `checkMesh` and inspect patch counts; then I will render the mesh surface to verify the seven passages visually.

The quality check passes, but the bounds show only one blade passage was retained; at this coarse resolution the narrow inlet annulus did not connect all seven passages. I will correct this in the mesh by supplying one keep-point in each passage via `locationsInMesh`, as requested, rather than revising the CAD.

Rather than accept seven artificially disconnected cell regions, I will make the coarsest useful correction: double the in-plane background resolution to 2.5 mm (1.25 mm at surfaces) and use one interior keep-point. The 4 mm inlet annulus should then remain connected around the hub and retain all seven passages. Root fillets remain omitted because 2 mm is still under two finest cells.

The corrected mesh now spans the full 116 mm diameter, is one region, has 29,831 cells, and passes `checkMesh`. I will render an oblique view of the boundary colored by patch to visually confirm the annular inlet, radial outlet, and seven curved blade passages.

The preview confirms all seven backward-curved passages and the named surfaces. Before closing, I need to make replay robust: some dictionary-writing cells also contained later failed commands and therefore were not retained. I will now emit one self-contained canonical final dictionary step, replacing all interim versions.

I will perform one final clean remesh from the canonical dictionaries, rerun `checkMesh`, and print the requested geometric measurements including an area/length verification of the constant 3 mm blade thickness.

The final case contains a 29,831-cell, single-region water mesh with separate `inlet`, `outlet`, `blades`, `backplate`, `hub`, and `shroud` patches. `checkMesh` reports **Mesh OK**.

Measured against the request:
- 7 blades: 7 built
- Backward sweep: 30.0° requested, 30.0° measured
- Blade thickness: 3.000 mm requested, 3.00009 mm measured
- Passage height: 14.0 mm requested, 14.0 mm measured
- Radial outlet: 58.0 mm requested, 58.0001 mm measured

Assumptions/changes:
- Interpreted the axial inlet as the annulus between the 12 mm hub and 16 mm blade leading radius.
- Added a 2 mm-long axial inlet neck solely to create distinct inlet and shroud CAD faces.
- Omitted the requested 2 mm blade-root fillets because the finest coarse-mesh cells are about 1.25 mm, leaving fewer than two cells across the fillet radius.
- The 60 mm backplate is solid hardware; the meshed water ends at the specified 58 mm radial blade outlet.
- No flow solution or boundary-condition setup was performed.
